title: Ordered degree-one coordinates trivialize the intrinsic affine-diagonal cone
statement: Let Y be any scheme and d a natural number. Write X for the ordered affine d-space tower over Y, p:X→Y for its projection [def-amb-affine-trace-tower, def-sbc-affine-space], W=X×_Y X, and s:X→W for the diagonal. For each i in Fin d let b_i be a section of the first power of the diagonal ideal whose inclusion into Γ(W,O_W) is p₂*(x_i)−p₁*(x_i). Form the homogeneous degree-one classes of these representatives in the actual conormal graded algebra [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]. Use the affine-morphism counit [def-pur-rees-cone-normalization, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] to view them as functions on the intrinsic relative-Spec normal cone [def-pur-normal-bundle]. The morphism from this cone to affine d-space over X with base map the cone projection and these ordered functions as coordinates is an isomorphism. This includes d=0, arbitrary rings of affine base charts, and empty Y. No extended-Rees comparison q or integration map occurs in this assertion.

source.place: Agreement on the model: the diagonal has the trivial normal bundle in ordered difference coordinates; expanded polynomial calculation of parent proof step 5

proof.text: At each point z of the affine tower choose the ambient affine neighborhood where the actual ordered coordinate differences regularly generate the diagonal ideal. Restrict the supplied representatives b_i to that neighborhood; naturality of powerInclusion and their prescribed global values give exactly these generators.

Use presentation.affineChart to identify the conormal algebra on the inverse-image affine with gr_J(R). The quotient-ring isomorphism for the surjective closed-immersion section map identifies R/J with the base sections. The regular-sequence graded-polynomial theorem makes evaluation at the homogeneous degree-one classes bijective. Compare constants using presentation.constants and degree-one variables using the affineChart representative formula; reindex Fin d by ULift. This is affineChart_eval_bijective.

Naturality of homogeneousClass and the relative-Spec counit identifies these local algebra coordinates with restrictions of the exact global cone functions in the conclusion. Transport the bijective polynomial evaluation along coneAlgebraIso and the open-section topIso maps. On an affine scheme, isoOfIsAffine and Gamma-Spec naturality make homOfVector an isomorphism whenever its polynomial evaluation is bijective.

The chosen inverse-image opens cover the diagonal source pointwise. Their affine spaces form an open cover of the target. The restriction of the global homOfVector is the local coordinate morphism by comp_homOfVector and homOfVector_comp_map. Each local map is an isomorphism by the previous step, so the Zariski-local isomorphism criterion proves the global map is an isomorphism. No assumption of a nonempty base or positive dimension was introduced.

theorem affineDiagonalGradedCoordinates_isIso (Y : Scheme.{u}) (d : ℕ)
    (b : (i : Fin d) → (ConormalGradedAlgebra.power
      (pullback.diagonal (affineTraceProjection Y d)) 1).val.obj (op ⊤))
    (_hb : ∀ i, (ConormalGradedAlgebra.powerInclusion
        (pullback.diagonal (affineTraceProjection Y d)) 1).val.app (op ⊤) (b i) =
      (pullback.snd (affineTraceProjection Y d) (affineTraceProjection Y d)).appTop
          (affineTraceCoordinate Y d i) -
        (pullback.fst (affineTraceProjection Y d) (affineTraceProjection Y d)).appTop
          (affineTraceCoordinate Y d i)) :
    let s := pullback.diagonal (affineTraceProjection Y d)
    let A := (ConormalGradedAlgebra.presentation s).algebra
    IsIso (AffineSpace.homOfVector (projection s)
      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin d) ↦
        let c := ConormalGradedAlgebra.homogeneousClass s A
          (ConormalGradedAlgebra.presentation s).inclusion 1 ⊤ (b i.down)
        let c' := A.right.obj.map (homOfLE (by simp)).op c
        (normalCone s).presheaf.map (homOfLE (by simp)).op
          ((Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.coneAlgebraIso s).hom.right.hom.app (op ⊤) c')))
